pageTitle: Klacks for mid-sized businesses | Scheduling when staff is short
metaDescription: Klacks for businesses with 50 to 250 employees: fill gaps in line with your rules, find the right replacement, scenarios instead of risk — no license fees.
hero.title: Fewer people, the same number of shifts.
hero.subtitle: Finding skilled staff is getting harder, the shifts stay. Klacks fills gaps in line with your rules and suggests a replacement who fits — so your scheduler gets more done in the same time.
hero.honesty: Klacks does not replace a scheduler. The rule-based planning engine calculates the plan, Klacksy takes over the clicking — you decide.
help.title: What takes work off your scheduler
help.items.0.title: Fill gaps in line with your rules
help.items.0.text: The planning assistant fills open shifts while keeping to your rules: rest periods, qualifications, availability. It plans in a scenario first — nothing is applied until you give your OK.
help.items.1.title: A replacement who fits
help.items.1.text: If someone drops out, ask Klacksy for a replacement. Only people who are not absent that day, have the required qualification, get no overlap and keep to the rest period are suggested — anyone with hours still open is listed higher up.
help.items.2.title: Scenarios instead of risk
help.items.2.text: For sickness absence or an order peak, you set up a scenario in advance. When it happens, you apply it instead of improvising under time pressure.
help.items.3.title: Clicking work by sentence
help.items.3.text: A sentence such as “Group all employees by qualification” is enough. Klacksy shows a preview and only carries it out after your yes.
help.items.4.title: Groups and locations
help.items.4.text: You model teams, locations and qualifications as groups — with Klacksy as well. You define per user who sees which groups.
help.items.5.title: Absences with clear responsibility
help.items.5.text: When an absence leaves a shift open, Klacks can ask the responsible schedulers one after another, via a connected messenger, who will take care of it — until someone takes over or the deadline expires.

needs.title: What you need
needs.server: A Linux server with at least 8 GB of memory and 4 CPU cores — or, to begin with, an office PC with Docker Desktop. Klacks installs new versions automatically.
needs.docker: Docker Desktop requires a paid license for companies with 250 or more employees or 10 million USD or more in annual revenue. If you are growing in that direction, you are better off planning a Linux server from the start.
agents.text: Already working with AI agents? Any agent that supports the open standard MCP (Model Context Protocol) can work directly with Klacks — only with the rights of the connected user.
